newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Macronix in T$200 bln wafer plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Macronix in T$200 bln wafer plan.

text.p: Taiwan semiconductor maker Macronix International Co said on Thursday it would invest more than T$200 billion within 10 years to build advanced 12-inch wafer fabrication plants.

The project involves an upgrading of an existing Macronix plant in Taiwan's main high-tech park at Hsinchu by adding a 12-inch production plant, the first such line at Hsinchu, company president Miin Wu told reporters.
In addition, Macronix will build two or three 12-inch wafer fabs at the fledgling Tainan Science-based Park in southern Tainan, Wu said.
The plants will be completed in 10 years or less, he said.
The Macronix move is the latest in a series of multibillion dollar microchip manufacturing projects announced by Taiwan's hotly competitive chipmakers.

While huge at T$200 billion (US$7 billion), the Macronix plan is dwarfed by 10-year development plans unveiled in recent months by market leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co and No.2 maker United Microelectronics.
Taiwan Semicon said in April it would spend T$400 billion to build six advanced production lines in the new Tainan park, the biggest single investment in Taiwan to date.
Arch rival United Micro went Taiwan Semicon one better in June, announcing a T$500 billion project to build 12-inch wafer fabs at Tainan.

Similarly advanced multibillion-dollar projects have been announced by Winbond Electronics Corp ; Nan Ya Technology, the chipmaking unit of Nan Ya Plastics ; Powerchip Co, a joint venture of Umax-Elite group and Mitsubishi Electric of Japan.
Macronix said the new production lines would enable it to produce a range of evolving products that are still in development, including one-gigibit mask ROM chips and 256-megabit flash memory chips.
Wu said Macronix was pouring more than 10 percent of its revenues into research and development.
